annotations.text:
Flow: Board (kanban + New from idea) -> live progress -> approve the publish -> diff review -> Push & open PR.
SimpleMode is the tray-badge ticket drafted in New from idea, seen by the non-developer who filed it — deliberately no sidebar. Its publish gate is HIGH, so it carries the same mandatory reject reason as the expert card, in plain language.

ApprovalPrompt = the HIGH-risk treatment only (publish gate; always an OS notification, mandatory reject reason, no Undo, no auto-allow).
MEDIUM is the compact inline card and LOW the passive line — both in TicketDetail's stream. The cumulative-risk strip in TicketDetail's rail promotes the next MEDIUM to HIGH: it is a weighted score, not a count — LOW +0.5, MEDIUM +1, a pre-commitment mismatch +3, HIGH +0 — over 10 segments, one per point of the threshold.

TicketDetail: use the "Needs you" switch to see #94 (in flight, click the stepper for phases), #98 at the plan-review gate, #108 pipenzo:awaiting-stack-approval, #113 pipenzo:needs-pre-scoping, #85 ci-failed, #87 with its activity stream still loading (id, stepper and rail come from the ticket store and render at once; only the stream replay is late).
#98 is the blocking half of the plan-review gate: Refine has finished and Implement will not start until the spec is approved, so the Refine step sits in its await state and the card carries acceptance criteria, an out-of-scope list, the files likely touched and the estimate.
Steer / Stop live under the stepper on #94's Refine, Implement and Review steps — not on Approve, where the run has already stopped. Stop asks first and keeps the commits. Approving the publish gate ends with the human-gated lesson prompt at the foot of the stream; a lesson saved there is reviewable and deletable in Settings.

Board: Working shows bounded concurrency (2 of 2 running, a held card with the file overlap, an approved stack as a container card). Both diff-gate outcomes land in Needs human, next to #92 pipenzo:interrupted, #101 pipenzo:merge-conflict — the second PR-event reaction, which parks here rather than in Ready for review because nothing has been attempted yet — and #89, the claim conflict: the loser of the best-effort assignment race, and the one card in the lane with no action, because someone else's claim is not yours to release. The sync pill's refresh steps through its three renderings: synced, syncing, syncing slowly.
Click the ⌘K field for the command palette and the workspace row for the connected-repos menu.

DiffReview: the right rail runs in order of authority — machine-verified gates, agent-captured evidence, then reviewer findings by severity. Click a finding to mark the line it names in the diff on the left. Critical is the only severity that holds the push gate closed; this run has none, which is why the gate list still reads 5/5 — build/typecheck, spec-generated tests, gitleaks, Semgrep and the diff-scope check, the same five Models locks. The diff-scope row reports the implementation diff and the generated test file separately, because a large generated test can never blow a ticket's estimate on its own.

Row 3: the four screens the sidebar has pointed at since the first pass and that were never built.
Connect is pre-app — no sidebar, like SimpleMode — and carries both device-flow steps: the code, then the picker whose selection becomes the workspace connected-repos list every other screen reads from.
Activity is what makes "the board shows open work, the history lives here" real: #105 merged, so GitHub closed it and its card left the board on the next poll — its publish, its gates and its refused worktree cleanup all stay in this feed.
Models & gates splits what is editable from what is not: routing classes pick a tier, verify is fixed at or above the implementer, and the five deterministic gates are switches you can read but not move. The task-type table under them is the second thing Refine emits — merge rate tracks task type, not diff size, so the tier floor and the gate strictness are read off both.
Settings carries the connected repos, concurrency, notification rules, the Simple/Expert default, the GitHub identity, and the saved lessons the ticket detail promises are reviewable and deletable here.

Foundations: "Loading, error and empty" is the section that covers what every other artboard skips — skeletons (one .sk shimmer primitive, flattened by the existing reduced-motion rule), pending buttons, the retrying vs blocking banner split, the schema-v2 read-only banner, pipenzo:interrupted in both its resumable (#92) and non-resumable (#93) forms, the refused worktree cleanup, and the first-run and per-lane empties.
Newer sections: Popovers (.pop, .cmdk-panel, .ws-menu), the native OS notification mock in Notices (the operating system's surface, not a fourth in-app altitude — three states reach it), live run controls, the plan-review gate, findings by severity, and lesson memory. The status-chip card states why there is no Done chip and no Done lane, and the PR-event reactions card says plainly that the third reaction, review comments, has no design yet.
